<mxfile host="Electron" scale="1" border="0"> <diagram name="Fan circuit" id="circuit_fan"> <mxGraphModel dx="1188" dy="815" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="900" pageHeight="600" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="title" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=18;fontStyle=1;" value="<b>Fan circuit</b> — spinning a motor (GPIO 18 & 19 → driver → motor)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="660" x="120" y="10" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="esp" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#30363d;strokeColor=#111;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=13;fontStyle=1;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=16;" value="

<mxGeometry height="24" width="94" x="166" y="235" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pinGND" parent="1" </mxCell> <mxCell id="wa" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=block;html=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#e07000;fontColor=#e07000;fontSize=9;" value="control signal"> <mxGeometry relative="1" <mxPoint x="320" y="312" /> </Array> <mxPoint x="226" y="312" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="360" y="300" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="gndshare" parent="1" style="text;html=1;fontSize=9;fontColor=#666;align=center;" value="shared GND" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="70" x="262" y="314" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="driver" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#c8e6c9;strokeColor=#2e7d32;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="

(battery / USB 5 V)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="160" x="360" y="380" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="powerw" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=block;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#e65100;fontColor=#e65100;fontSize=9;" value="big current"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="440" y="380" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="440" y="350" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="mwa" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=none;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#444;"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="520" y="210" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="640" y="210" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="mwb" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=none;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#444;"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <Array as="points"> <mxPoint x="600" y="290" /> <mxPoint x="600" y="270" /> </Array> <mxPoint x="520" y="290" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="640" y="270" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="motor" parent="1" style="ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#bbdefb;strokeColor=#1565c0;fontSize=13;fontStyle=1;" value="M
🌀
fan motor" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="90" x="640" y="200" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="spin" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=10;fontStyle=2;fontColor=#1565c0;" value="spins! (reverse the two
signals → spins the other way)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="180" x="600" y="300" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="phys" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#eef6ff;strokeColor=#4a90d9;fontSize=12;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;" value="⚡ <b>Physics:</b> a motor is a coil of wire that becomes an electromagnet and spins against magnets. It needs FAR more current than a GPIO pin can safely give (a pin gives a whisper; a motor wants a shout), and when it spins it kicks voltage back ("back-EMF") that would fry the ESP32. So the pin never powers the motor directly. Instead GPIO 18/19 send tiny <b>control signals</b> to a <b>motor driver (H-bridge)</b>, which uses its own power supply to push the big current. A=on,B=off spins one way; swap them to reverse; PWM sets the speed." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="800" x="50" y="450" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: ⚡ Physics: a motor is a coil of wire that becomes an electromagnet and spins against magnets. It needs FAR more current than a GPIO pin can safely give (a pin gives a whisper; a motor wants a shout), and when it spins it kicks voltage back ("back-EMF") that would fry the ESP32. So the pin never powers the motor directly. Instead GPIO 18/19 send tiny control signals to a motor driver (H-bridge), which uses its own power supply to push the big current. A=on,B=off spins one way; swap them to reverse; PWM sets the speed.
